title: Consistency of Safety Across Decoding Parameters: Temperature, Top-p, and Repetition Penalty

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: many applications expose decoding parameters to users. If safety collapses at common high-temperature settings, this is a practical deployment risk with an easy fix (constrain parameter ranges). Actionable and specific.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Sweeping decoding parameters (temperature, top-p, repetition penalty) and measuring ASR is straightforward scripting. Uses standard HuggingFace generation APIs. No ML training needed. Highly beginner-friendly.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: a heatmap of ASR across parameter grid for each model. Can be scoped to 2-3 models. Grid search is systematic and automatable. Fits well in 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: This idea is largely addressed by 'Catastrophic Jailbreak of Open-source LLMs via Exploiting Generation' (Huang et al., ICLR 2024), which demonstrated that varying decoding hyper-parameters (temperature, top-p, top-k sampling) increases attack success rate from 0% to 95%+ across 11 language models. The paper systematically sweeps generation configurations and measures safety degradation, which is essentially the proposed experiment. SafeDecoding (ACL 2024) provides the defense counterpart. The proposed heatmap deliverable would replicate existing findings with minor extensions (repetition penalty parameter, updated models).
